rejected.title: Prim's algorithm
card: A minimum spanning tree joins every vertex of a weighted graph using the smallest possible total weight. Prim's algorithm builds one step by step.
Start at any vertex. Look at all the edges that join a vertex in the tree to a vertex not yet in the tree. Add the cheapest one.
Repeat until every vertex is in the tree. A graph with n vertices needs n − 1 edges. If two edges tie, either can be chosen, and the total weight is the same.
Example: edges AB = 4, AC = 2, BC = 3, BD = 5, CD = 6. Start at A and add AC (2). Then add BC (3), which brings in B. Then add BD (5), which brings in D. Total = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.
rejected.remember: Always add the cheapest edge that reaches a new vertex, and stop at n − 1 edges.

a.q: A tree has A and C so far. Edges from the tree to new vertices are AB = 4, CB = 3, CD = 6. Which edge does Prim's algorithm add next?
a.why: Prim's algorithm adds the cheapest edge that joins a new vertex to the tree. Of the edges that reach B or D, CB at 3 is the smallest. AC is not an option because both A and C are already in the tree.
a.clue: The edge must reach a vertex that is not yet in the tree.

b.q: A network has edges PQ = 5, PR = 3, QR = 2, QS = 6, RS = 4, RT = 7, ST = 3. Using Prim's algorithm from P, what is the total weight of the minimum spanning tree?
b.why: From P add PR (3). Then QR (2), then RS (4), then ST (3). That is 4 edges for 5 vertices, and 3 + 2 + 4 + 3 = 12. A total of 15 comes from taking PQ (5) instead of QR (2) at the second step, but QR is cheaper and also brings in Q.
b.clue: At each step, list only the edges that reach a new vertex, then pick the smallest.
